## Game idea
Cube Cash Tycoon, a Roblox multiplayer tycoon (rebuild of an existing game). Existing systems: a central plaza with 6 themed claimable plots (Candy, Lava, Ice, Jungle, Neon City, Desert); droppers drop ore onto a conveyor into a collector that pays cash; a data-driven upgrade tree (4 dropper slots, ore tiers Bronze/Silver/Gold/Diamond, conveyor speed, cash multipliers) bought on BuyPads or in a SHOP panel; rebirth with a permanent multiplier; cash-in VFX and sounds; an in-world TOP TYCOONS leaderboard; a first-60-seconds tutorial arrow; DataStore saving. The server already bumps these ForgeTelemetry counters, so the first_60_seconds beats MUST use only these names: plaza_built, themes_built, plots_claimed, auto_claims, cubes_dropped, cubes_collected, cashin_fx_sent, upgrades_bought, tier_upgrades, purchase_fx_sent, shop_opened, shop_purchases, tutorial_steps, rebirths, leaderboard_refresh, data_loaded, data_saved.

## Curated genre lessons
# Roblox tycoon best practices
- Give the player their own plot instantly on join (auto-claim, or a big glowing CLAIM pad beside spawn) and teleport them onto it.
- Core loop: droppers spawn ore parts that roll along a conveyor into a collector that pays cash; the player walks onto buy pads to unlock the next item. The first dropper is FREE or costs what the player earns in ~5 seconds.
- Use 3+ dropper tiers (different colours and values), conveyor speed upgrades, a collector multiplier and decorative unlocks (walls, floor, lamps, sign) so the plot visibly grows from bare to busy.
- Buy pads: a Neon pad with a PriceBillboard, green when affordable and red when not; only the next 1-3 pads are visible so the path is obvious. On purchase the pad vanishes with a pop, the unlocked model rises/scales in with a Back tween, sparkles burst, a purchase sound plays and the cash counter punches.
- Rebirth: at a cash threshold, reset cash and unlocks for a permanent multiplier (x1.5, x2, ...); show the requirement as a progress bar and celebrate with a RewardPopup plus a camera shake.
- Upgrade tree: 3 branches (income, speed, luck), each with 3-5 levels and growing costs, shown in a Panel with StyledButtons.
- Leaderboard: leaderstats Cash and Rebirths, plus a top-players board (HUD or in-world).
- Economy pacing: the next purchase is reachable in 15-40 s early on; costs x1.4 per step; income per second is visible on the HUD ("+$12/s").
- Collector feedback: each ore collected flashes the collector, plays a soft tick and shows "+$N" floating text; batch client updates (at most ~10 remote events per second).
- Server-authoritative cash; buy pads check cash and plot ownership on the server; ore parts are destroyed on collection and capped (e.g. 60 live ores per plot) so the server never lags.
- Telemetry counters: plot_claimed, ore_spawned, ore_collected, cash_earned, item_bought, upgrade_bought, rebirth.

# Fun-first rules (every game)
- The first 10 seconds decide everything: the player spawns facing the core action, sees one glowing obvious thing to do, and gets a reward for doing it within 5 seconds.
- Every player action gets layered feedback: a sound, a particle burst or flash, a UI punch/tween, and a number change. Big moments (unlock, level up, rebirth, win) add a camera shake and a centre RewardPopup.
- Numbers go up visibly: leaderstats plus a HUD counter that ticks up and pops; show "+N" floating text where the reward happened.
- Always show the next goal: a progress bar or a price tag that turns green when affordable, so the player always knows what to save for.
- Pace: a new unlock or upgrade every 20-40 seconds in the first 3 minutes, then slower; costs grow ~1.3-1.6x per step and income grows with them.
- No placeholder grey: every part sets Color and Material from one bright palette (SmoothPlastic, Neon accents, Wood/Grass/Brick/Slate for ground and walls). Set Lighting (ClockTime ~14, Brightness 2-3, an Atmosphere, Bloom and a ColorCorrection with Saturation ~0.15) so the world pops.
- Sounds: one short sound per action (collect, buy, error, unlock, jump pad) and soft looping music at low volume. UI sounds play on the client (SoundService:PlayLocalSound); world sounds are parented to the part. Use the game's sound table, never invented asset ids.
- Rewards without monetisation: a free timed gift every few minutes, streak multipliers, cosmetic unlocks (trails, colours), a rebirth multiplier, achievements shown as toasts.
- Readable world: a sign or BillboardGui on every interactive object; interactive things glow (Neon or a Highlight) or bob/spin with a tween.
- Solo-playable: everything works with one player; a leaderboard still shows the solo player.

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value.
- Touched fires many times per touch: debounce per player (a per-player cooldown or a one-time purchased flag) and check and deduct cost in the same step to prevent double-buys or double-spends.
- Define the data shape that a builder module returns (field names such as origin, gate, spawn) once, and have consumers use those exact fields. Do not add `a or b` fallbacks for guessed names.

## Fixing and debugging
- A "sync" StudioError about not being able to serve a path is an infrastructure or environment failure, not a code bug. Do not change game code in response. Retry the step.
- If the critic says a code path was never exercised in the playtest, fix the pacing or setup so the path actually runs (e.g. cheaper first purchase) instead of only adding more code.
- When the spec changes the flow (e.g. from auto-assign to claim), rewrite the entry script (Game.server) to require and wire the new modules, and delete the old flow's logic (slots, teleport on join). Updating only the new modules leaves the old behaviour running.
- After a redesign, check that every module is required by the entry script and that its init function is called. Unwired modules never run, and their counters never fire.

## Sound table (ReplicatedStorage/GameAssets.luau: GameAssets.play(name, parentOrNil))
- Coin: short bright tick-ding for coins, cash, pickups
- Buy: purchase confirm for buy pads and shop buttons
- Click: UI button click
- Pop: soft pop for things appearing
- Error: can't do that: not enough cash, locked
- Whoosh: whoosh for jump pads, dashes, teleports, panels opening
- Jump: character jump / bounce
- Land: landing thud, heavy object placed
- Boom: big moment: rebirth, explosion, level up
- Splash: water splash, liquid, slime
- Hurt: player hurt or touched a kill brick
- Win: checkpoint / reward / win sting
- Music: looping background music (empty until a verified id is added; music() is then a no-op)

## UI kit the coder gets (name the ones a client module needs in its purpose)
- ChunkyText: Any TextLabel players must read: titles, labels, timers, status text.
- StyledButton: Every clickable: buy, upgrade, play, claim, open shop, rebirth, toggle.
- Panel: A window: shop, inventory, upgrades, settings, quests, with close X and dim backdrop.
- Toast: Short notifications: earned coins, not enough cash, round started, unlocked.
- CurrencyCounter: HUD pill for coins/gems/cash bound to a leaderstat; number ticks up and pops.
- ProgressBar: XP, level, health, stamina, timer, capacity or goal progress bar with shine sweep.
- RewardPopup: Big centre celebration: level up, chest/egg opened, unlock, win, rebirth.
- PriceBillboard: World price tag on a buy pad / shop item (BillboardGui), green when affordable. Works in server Scripts.
- FloatingText: Rising '+1' / '+$50' text over a world point for pickups, hits and payouts (client).
- Leaderboard: Live top-players HUD panel sorted by a leaderstat (cash, stage, rebirths), local player highlighted.
- ShopGrid: Grid of item/upgrade cards (emoji icon, name, price, level x/max, buy button) inside a shop or upgrade Panel.
- RebirthPanel: Rebirth/prestige card: requirement progress bar, x current -> x next multiplier, pulsing button when ready.
- BuyPad: Glowing step-on pad that buys/unlocks the next item (droppers, walls, upgrades, zones), bobbing price, debounce. Server Script.
